privacy_note: aggregates only -- no message text, phone numbers, handles, or names below or anywhere in the script's output
tapback_filter_note: F1 fix (2026-09-05): rows with a non-zero associated_message_type (tapback reactions, e.g. 2000-2006 for heart/like/etc.) are excluded from both the reply side and the initiation side via load_dm_messages_excluding_tapbacks(). All numbers below are POST-fix; the pre-fix numbers are preserved verbatim under before_tapback_filter for the record.

sensitivity_table.note: each row is an independent invocation of the shipped script with --gap-hours (INITIATION_GAP_HOURS override) and --fir-window-hours varied; --min-n lowered to 1 for this table only, so every cell is shown even where it would fall below the production refusal floor of 30. Rate is not sensitive to fir_window_hours beyond ~24h (0 rows move at gap_hours>=6, post-filter); it IS sensitive to gap_hours, consistent with a larger silence-gap threshold selecting fewer, more genuinely cold openers. Re-measured 2026-09-05 with the tapback filter applied (Finding F1) -- n and unanswered both drop slightly vs before_tapback_filter below (tapback rows were ~3.8% of in-window DM rows), rate moves by <=0.02 in every cell.

recommended_pair.reason: gap_hours=6 mirrors eval_when_to_speak.py's --seth-already-engaged-hours default; fir_window_hours=24 is FIR_WINDOW_HOURS, the imported comparison window shared with eval_when_to_speak.py's own FIR (AC-3.1).

before_tapback_filter.note: Pre-F1-fix numbers, kept verbatim for the record. These were measured against load_dm_messages() (no associated_message_type filter), which counted a subset of bare tapback reactions as replies on the reply side and as initiations on the initiation side.

retention_floor_note: the available n above rolls forward roughly one day per day (chat.db's Keep-Messages retention window); a future run will not reproduce this exact date_range or n -- see design doc Finding 2. The refusal floor (n < 30, AC-3.3) is a real possible future outcome, not just a test fixture.
scope_note: per designs/US-3.md's Scope note: AC-3.1-AC-3.6 define exactly one metric (the false-initiation / unanswered rate for Seth's own openers), reusing scripts/blind_ab/score.py's wilson() for the CI per AC-3.4's explicit 'do not reimplement' instruction. There is no separate Seth-side MIR/missed-response metric in this story's scope -- see the design doc for why that is a distinct, similarly-sized follow-up rather than an add-on here.
